name: cflow
desc: Generate call graphs from C code
why: GNU call graph generator for C code; a useful lens for seeing how a codebase's control flow actually fits together.

brief.what_it_is: GNU cflow is a command-line tool that takes a collection of C source files and prints a graph of the control flow within the program. It can produce direct flowgraphs (who calls whom) or inverted ones (who is called by whom), and can optionally add a cross-reference listing. Output comes in two formats, POSIX and GNU (extended). The package also ships an Emacs major mode for browsing the generated flowcharts inside Emacs.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames it as a GNU Project tool for charting control flow in C programs, part of the free-software toolkit. The homepage does not spell out a deeper motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the mechanism. It says cflow analyzes C source files and prints a graph, and that direct and inverted flowgraphs and an optional cross-reference listing can be generated. Details would be in the manual, which the page points to via info and man.

commands_seen.context: The homepage's pointer to a brief usage summary of the tool.
Opens the full cflow documentation in the GNU info reader.
Imports the GPG key that signs release tarballs from version 1.8 onward, so you can verify a download.
Checks the signature on the cflow-1.8 release tarball against the imported key.

brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the usual package install is described on the homepage. For verifying a source tarball, you need gpg and the maintainer's key, which the page says to import from keyserver.ubuntu.com. Releases up to 1.7 were signed with a different key, listed on the page. Source tarballs come from the GNU FTP server or its mirrors.
brief.standout: Nothing on the homepage is clearly unusual. It is a classic GNU tool that does one job, and its two output formats and Emacs integration are the notable parts.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows a named maintainer (Sergey Poznyakoff), a release 1.8 with a newer signing key, and a page update stamp of 2025/07/30. It gives no explicit last-release date or commit history, and I did not check the savannah project page.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not list supported platforms, build requirements, or a feature list beyond the outputs. It has no sample output inline; it links to an online sample flowchart whose URL I did not see in the page text. Licensed under GPL v3 or later.
quotes: GNU cflow analyzes a collection of C source files and prints a graph, charting control flow within the program.
Two output formats are implemented: POSIX and GNU (extended).
The package also provides Emacs major mode for examining the produced flowcharts in Emacs.
